ingredients.name: Whole grain oats
ingredients.summary: Whole grain oats are a minimally processed cereal grain that provides fiber, vitamins, and minerals, and are generally considered safe and health-promoting for most people.
ingredients.details: Whole grain oats contain beta-glucan fiber, which can help support healthy cholesterol levels and blood sugar control, and they provide complex carbohydrates, protein, and micronutrients. The main concern is for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity, as oats can be cross-contaminated with gluten-containing grains unless specifically labeled gluten-free. Overall, they are a nutrient-dense ingredient with no added additives, sweeteners, or preservatives indicated here.

ingredients.name: Cereal flakes
ingredients.summary: Cereal flakes are typically made from processed grains such as corn, wheat, oats, or rice and are generally considered safe for most people. The health impact depends on whether they are whole grain and how much sugar or sodium is added in the final product.
ingredients.details: If the flakes are whole grain and minimally sweetened, they can provide fiber, vitamins, and minerals and are usually a healthy option. However, some flake cereals can be highly processed and contain added sugars, salt, and flavorings, which may contribute to weight gain, blood sugar spikes, and higher sodium intake if eaten in large amounts. People with gluten intolerance or celiac disease should check whether the flakes are made from gluten-containing grains such as wheat or barley.

ingredients.name: Flax seeds
ingredients.summary: Flax seeds are nutrient-dense seeds rich in fiber and omega-3 fatty acids and are generally considered safe and beneficial for most people. They are often used to support heart and digestive health.
ingredients.details: Flax seeds provide alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), a plant-based omega-3, as well as lignans and soluble and insoluble fiber, which can help improve cholesterol levels and support regular bowel movements. Very high intakes without enough water may cause digestive discomfort or constipation, and people on blood-thinning medications or with certain hormone-sensitive conditions should discuss large supplemental use with a healthcare provider. Whole flax seeds may pass through the gut undigested, so ground flax is often better for nutrient absorption.

ingredients.name: Chia seeds
ingredients.summary: Chia seeds are small seeds high in fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, and minerals and are generally considered safe and health-promoting. They are commonly used to support heart health, satiety, and blood sugar control.
ingredients.details: Chia seeds absorb water and form a gel, which can slow digestion, promote fullness, and help stabilize blood sugar levels. Their high fiber content supports digestive health, but sudden large intakes without adequate fluids can cause bloating or constipation in some people. Individuals with swallowing difficulties should be cautious and ensure chia seeds are pre-soaked or mixed into moist foods to reduce choking risk.

ingredients.name: Quinoa
ingredients.summary: Quinoa is a whole grain seed rich in protein, fiber, and minerals, and is generally considered a very healthy food ingredient.
ingredients.details: Quinoa is naturally gluten-free and provides complete protein with all essential amino acids, along with fiber, magnesium, and other micronutrients. It is well tolerated by most people; main concerns are limited to rare allergies or digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals, especially if not rinsed properly to remove natural saponins.

ingredients.name: Amaranth flakes
ingredients.summary: Amaranth flakes are processed from the amaranth grain, a nutrient-dense, gluten-free pseudocereal used as a whole-grain ingredient.
ingredients.details: Amaranth is high in protein, fiber, and minerals such as iron and magnesium, and is naturally gluten-free, making it suitable for many people with gluten intolerance or celiac disease. Health concerns are minimal; as with other high-fiber grains, excessive intake may cause mild digestive discomfort in some individuals, but it does not contain common problematic additives, artificial colors, or preservatives.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.summary: Palm oil is a common cooking and frying oil high in saturated fat, which can negatively affect heart health when consumed in excess.
ingredients.details: Palm oil is widely used in processed foods because it is cheap and stable at high temperatures. It is relatively high in saturated fat, which can raise LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and potentially increase cardiovascular risk when eaten frequently. Occasional intake in the context of an overall healthy diet is generally considered acceptable, but heavy reliance on palm-oil-rich processed foods is not ideal.

ingredients.name: Canola oil
ingredients.summary: Canola oil is a vegetable oil relatively low in saturated fat and commonly used for cooking and in processed foods.
ingredients.details: Canola oil contains mostly monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, including some omega‑3 fatty acids. In typical amounts, it is generally considered heart‑healthier than more saturated fats like palm or coconut oil. Health concerns mainly arise when it is heavily refined and used in large amounts in ultra‑processed foods, rather than from moderate use in home cooking.

ingredients.name: Soy lecithin
ingredients.summary: Soy lecithin is an emulsifier derived from soy that helps blend fats and water in processed foods.
ingredients.details: Soy lecithin is used in small amounts to improve texture and prevent separation in foods like chocolate, baked goods, and sauces. It is generally recognized as safe, and the residual soy protein is usually very low, so most people with soy allergy tolerate it, though highly sensitive individuals should still be cautious. It does not significantly contribute to overall soy intake or hormones.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.summary: Wheat flour is a refined grain ingredient that contains gluten and can impact blood sugar when consumed in large amounts.
ingredients.details: Refined wheat flour is low in fiber and can cause rapid increases in blood glucose, which may contribute to weight gain and metabolic issues if eaten frequently. It contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity. Whole‑grain alternatives are generally more nutritious due to higher fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.summary: Sugar is a simple carbohydrate that adds sweetness but no essential nutrients, and excessive intake is linked to multiple health issues.
ingredients.details: High intake of added sugars is associated with increased risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and dental cavities. It can also contribute to blood sugar spikes and cravings, especially when combined with refined flours and fats in processed foods. Occasional small amounts are generally fine, but frequent consumption of sugar‑rich products is a concern.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.summary: Salt (sodium chloride) is necessary in small amounts but can raise blood pressure when consumed in excess.
ingredients.details: Processed foods are a major source of dietary sodium, and high sodium intake is strongly linked to hypertension and increased risk of heart disease and stroke. People with high blood pressure, kidney disease, or salt sensitivity should be particularly cautious. The overall risk depends on total daily sodium from all foods, not just this product alone.

ingredients.name: Corn starch
ingredients.summary: Corn starch is a refined carbohydrate used as a thickener and texture agent in many foods.
ingredients.details: Corn starch is mostly pure starch and provides calories without significant vitamins, minerals, or fiber. In moderate amounts it is generally safe, but like other refined starches it can contribute to rapid blood sugar increases when eaten in large quantities. It is typically gluten‑free, which may be suitable for those avoiding gluten, assuming no cross‑contamination.

ingredients.name: Spices
ingredients.summary: Spices are flavoring ingredients derived from plants and are generally safe, often providing beneficial phytonutrients.
ingredients.details: The term “spices” is broad and may include ingredients like pepper, paprika, cumin, or others, depending on the recipe. Most culinary spices are associated with antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties and are safe for most people. Rarely, individuals may react to specific spices, but this is uncommon compared with major allergens like nuts or dairy.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.summary: Garlic is a natural flavoring ingredient that may offer cardiovascular and immune benefits.
ingredients.details: Garlic contains sulfur compounds that have been studied for potential cholesterol‑lowering, blood pressure‑modulating, and antimicrobial effects. It is generally safe when consumed in typical food amounts, though large quantities may cause digestive discomfort in some people. Those with garlic intolerance or certain FODMAP sensitivities may need to limit it.

ingredients.name: Whole milk powder
ingredients.summary: Whole milk powder is dehydrated milk containing lactose and milk proteins, including fat, and is a dairy allergen.
ingredients.details: Whole milk powder provides protein, calcium, and fat, but it is a clear concern for people with cow’s milk allergy or lactose intolerance. The saturated fat content may contribute to higher LDL cholesterol in some individuals if consumed in large amounts. For most people, moderate dairy intake can fit into a balanced diet, but those with dairy sensitivities should avoid it.

ingredients.name: Skim milk powder
ingredients.summary: Skim milk powder is dehydrated low‑fat milk that still contains lactose and milk proteins, making it a dairy allergen.
ingredients.details: Skim milk powder offers protein and calcium with less fat than whole milk powder, but it still poses a risk for individuals with milk allergy or lactose intolerance. It can contribute to overall protein and nutrient intake in the diet. As with other dairy ingredients, the main concerns are for those with allergies, intolerances, or those deliberately limiting dairy.

ingredients.name: Caramel color
ingredients.summary: Caramel color is a common brown food coloring made by heating sugars, and some types may contain trace levels of potentially harmful by‑products.
ingredients.details: Caramel color is widely used in sauces, soft drinks, and processed foods to give a brown appearance. Certain classes (especially Class III and IV) can contain 4‑methylimidazole (4‑MEI), a compound that has raised cancer concerns in animal studies, though typical dietary exposures are generally low. Regulatory agencies set limits, but people aiming to minimize exposure to unnecessary additives may choose to limit products with caramel color.

ingredients.name: Monosodium glutamate
ingredients.summary: Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is a flavor enhancer that intensifies savory (umami) taste. It is generally recognized as safe, but some people report sensitivity symptoms such as headache or flushing.
ingredients.details: MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid and is widely used in processed foods and seasonings to boost flavor. Regulatory agencies consider it safe at typical intake levels, but a subset of individuals may experience short‑term symptoms sometimes referred to as 'MSG symptom complex.' It can also contribute modestly to overall sodium intake, which is relevant for people managing blood pressure or heart disease.

ingredients.name: Defatted soybean
ingredients.summary: Defatted soybean is soy from which most of the oil has been removed, leaving a protein‑rich ingredient. It is a common source of plant protein and a major soy allergen.
ingredients.details: This ingredient is often used in processed foods to increase protein content and improve texture. Soy is generally considered heart‑healthy due to its unsaturated fats and protein profile, but defatted forms are more about protein than fat. However, soy is one of the top food allergens and can cause reactions ranging from mild to severe in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Yeast extract
ingredients.summary: Yeast extract is a flavoring made from broken‑down yeast cells that naturally contains glutamates, enhancing savory taste. It is often used as a cleaner‑label alternative to MSG but can have similar flavor‑enhancing effects.
ingredients.details: Because yeast extract is rich in free glutamic acid, it can intensify umami flavor in soups, snacks, and seasonings. While considered safe for most people, individuals who are sensitive to glutamates or who try to avoid MSG‑like ingredients may also react to yeast extract. It can also contribute small amounts of sodium depending on formulation.

ingredients.name: Natural and artificial flavors
ingredients.summary: Natural and artificial flavors are blended chemicals used to create or boost taste, with 'natural' derived from natural sources and 'artificial' synthesized. Their exact composition is usually not disclosed.
ingredients.details: These flavorings can include dozens of compounds, solvents, and carriers, all generally approved for food use. While typically safe at the levels used, the lack of transparency makes it difficult for consumers to know exactly what they are ingesting, which can be a concern for people with chemical sensitivities or specific intolerances. Artificial flavors also indicate a higher degree of processing and formulation in the product.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.summary: Honey is a natural sweetener composed mainly of fructose and glucose. It adds calories and sugar but also contains small amounts of antioxidants and trace compounds.
ingredients.details: From a health perspective, honey behaves similarly to other sugars in terms of blood sugar impact and calorie contribution, so it should be used in moderation, especially for people with diabetes or those managing weight. It is not suitable for infants under one year due to the risk of infant botulism. For most older children and adults, moderate intake is considered safe.

ingredients.name: Dextrin
ingredients.summary: Dextrin is a group of short‑chain carbohydrates produced from starch, used as a thickener, filler, or carrier. It is generally recognized as safe but adds easily digestible carbohydrates.
ingredients.details: Dextrin is quickly broken down into glucose in the digestive tract, contributing to carbohydrate and calorie intake and potentially affecting blood sugar. It is often used in powdered seasonings and processed foods to improve texture or help disperse flavors. For most people it is safe, but those managing blood sugar or following low‑carb diets may want to monitor intake.

ingredients.name: Pasteurized milk
ingredients.summary: Pasteurized milk is cow’s milk that has been heat‑treated to kill harmful bacteria. It is a common source of protein, calcium, and lactose, and is a major allergen.
ingredients.details: Pasteurization improves safety by reducing the risk of foodborne illness without significantly changing the basic nutritional profile. Milk provides beneficial nutrients but also contains lactose, which can cause digestive symptoms in lactose‑intolerant individuals, and milk proteins that can trigger allergic reactions. For people without these issues, it is generally safe when consumed in moderation.

ingredients.name: Cheese cultures
ingredients.summary: Cheese cultures are specific bacteria used to ferment milk and develop cheese flavor and texture. They are generally safe and commonly used in dairy processing.
ingredients.details: These bacterial cultures help convert lactose into lactic acid and produce characteristic flavors and textures in cheese and related products. They may slightly reduce lactose content but do not remove it entirely, so the product can still affect those with lactose intolerance or milk allergy. For most consumers, cheese cultures pose no health risk and may even contribute beneficial bacteria depending on processing.

ingredients.name: Enzymes
ingredients.summary: Enzymes are proteins used in food processing to modify texture, flavor, or structure, such as in cheese making. They are typically present in very small amounts and are considered safe for most people.
ingredients.details: In dairy products, enzymes like rennet help coagulate milk and develop cheese structure and flavor. Although they are processing aids and used in tiny quantities, some enzymes can be derived from animal, microbial, or fungal sources, which may matter for vegetarians, vegans, or those with specific religious dietary rules. Allergic reactions are rare but possible in highly sensitive individuals, mainly among workers with occupational exposure.

ingredients.name: Onion flake
ingredients.summary: Onion flake is dehydrated onion used for flavoring.
ingredients.details: Dehydrated onion provides natural onion flavor and some phytonutrients, though many heat-sensitive compounds are reduced during processing. It is generally safe for most people, but those with onion or allium sensitivities or certain digestive conditions (such as FODMAP sensitivity) may experience gastrointestinal discomfort. It does not add significant additives or unhealthy fats.

ingredients.name: Natural flavor
ingredients.summary: Natural flavor is a broad term for flavoring substances derived from natural sources but often highly processed and not fully disclosed.
ingredients.details: “Natural flavor” can include complex mixtures of compounds extracted or derived from plant or animal sources, and may contain solvents, carriers, or processing aids not individually listed. While legally distinct from artificial flavors, both can be similarly processed and may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals (e.g., to certain botanicals or hidden allergens). The lack of specificity makes it difficult for consumers with allergies, migraines, or chemical sensitivities to assess risk accurately.

ingredients.name: Onion extract
ingredients.summary: Onion extract is a concentrated form of onion used to boost savory flavor.
ingredients.details: Onion extract is typically produced by concentrating onion juice or flavor compounds, providing strong onion taste without bulk. It is generally safe, but like other onion ingredients, it may cause digestive discomfort in individuals with allium or FODMAP sensitivities. It does not inherently introduce artificial additives, though it may be part of complex flavor systems in some products.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce (soybean, wheat, salt)
ingredients.summary: Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning made from soybeans, wheat, and salt; it is high in sodium and contains major allergens (soy and wheat/gluten).
ingredients.details: Traditional soy sauce is produced by fermenting soybeans and wheat with salt, creating a rich umami flavor but also a high sodium content that can contribute to elevated blood pressure when consumed frequently. It contains both soy and wheat, making it unsuitable for people with soy allergy, wheat allergy, or celiac disease/gluten intolerance. Fermented products are generally safe, but sensitive individuals should monitor total sodium and allergen exposure.

ingredients.name: Garlic extract
ingredients.summary: Garlic extract is a concentrated garlic flavoring used to enhance savory taste.
ingredients.details: Garlic extract provides the characteristic flavor and some bioactive compounds of garlic, though processing can alter its exact composition. It is generally safe and may even have beneficial cardiovascular effects in whole-food forms, but in concentrated or extract form it mainly serves as flavor. Individuals with garlic or allium sensitivities or certain digestive issues (e.g., FODMAP intolerance) may experience discomfort and should monitor intake.

ingredients.name: Tomato powder
ingredients.summary: Tomato powder is dehydrated, ground tomato used for flavor and color. It is essentially a concentrated whole-food ingredient.
ingredients.details: Tomato powder retains many of the nutrients and phytochemicals of fresh tomatoes, including lycopene and some vitamins. Health concerns are minimal unless someone has a tomato allergy or needs to limit acidic foods. It can contribute small amounts of natural sugars and potassium but is generally considered a wholesome ingredient.

ingredients.name: Dried onion
ingredients.summary: Dried onion is dehydrated onion used as a seasoning. It is a minimally processed vegetable ingredient.
ingredients.details: Drying removes water but preserves much of the flavor compounds and some beneficial phytochemicals found in fresh onion. It is generally safe, with the main issues being intolerance in people sensitive to alliums (onion, garlic) or those with digestive conditions triggered by FODMAPs. It does not typically introduce additives or significant health risks.

ingredients.name: Glucose
ingredients.summary: Glucose is a simple sugar used as a sweetener and energy source. High intake of added sugars like glucose is linked to metabolic health issues.
ingredients.details: Glucose rapidly raises blood sugar and insulin levels, which can be problematic for people with insulin resistance, prediabetes, or diabetes. Regular high consumption of added sugars contributes to weight gain, fatty liver, and increased cardiovascular risk. In small amounts within an overall low-sugar diet it is acceptable, but frequent exposure from many products is a concern.

ingredients.name: Sucrose fatty acid esters
ingredients.summary: Sucrose fatty acid esters are emulsifiers made from sugar and fatty acids, used to blend fats and water. They are approved food additives and generally considered safe at typical intake levels.
ingredients.details: These emulsifiers help stabilize textures in processed foods and are metabolized into sucrose and fatty acids in the body. Regulatory agencies have set acceptable daily intake levels based on toxicology data showing low toxicity. Some emerging research suggests that frequent consumption of multiple emulsifiers may affect gut microbiota in susceptible individuals, but current evidence for this specific additive is limited.

ingredients.name: Dextrose (anhydrous glucose)
ingredients.summary: Dextrose (anhydrous glucose) is a form of glucose used as a sweetener and bulking agent. Like other added sugars, high intake is associated with metabolic health risks.
ingredients.details: Chemically, dextrose is D-glucose and is quickly absorbed, causing rapid increases in blood sugar and insulin. Frequent consumption of foods high in dextrose and other added sugars contributes to weight gain, insulin resistance, and increased risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease. While a single product may not be harmful on its own, cumulative intake from many processed foods is the main concern.

ingredients.name: Banana
ingredients.summary: Banana in ingredient form usually refers to dried or processed banana used for flavor and sweetness. It is a whole-food fruit ingredient.
ingredients.details: Banana provides natural sugars, fiber (if not fully strained), potassium, and various vitamins. In processed foods, the amount may be small, but it is generally considered a wholesome component compared with refined sweeteners. The main concern would be for individuals with specific fruit allergies or those who must tightly control carbohydrate intake.

ingredients.name: Processed honey
ingredients.summary: Processed honey is refined or heat-treated honey used as a sweetener. Despite its natural origin, it is still a concentrated source of sugars.
ingredients.details: Processing can reduce some of honey’s beneficial enzymes and phytochemicals, making it nutritionally closer to other added sugars. It is primarily composed of fructose and glucose and contributes to total added sugar intake, with similar metabolic effects to other sweeteners when consumed in excess. It should be avoided in infants under one year due to the risk of botulism, and adults should still treat it as an added sugar.

ingredients.name: Tomato paste
ingredients.summary: Concentrated tomato product used for flavor and color, generally considered safe and nutritious.
ingredients.details: Tomato paste is made by cooking and concentrating tomatoes, providing natural lycopene, vitamins, and minerals. For most people it is a low‑risk ingredient; only individuals with tomato allergy, reflux, or sensitivity to acidic foods may need to limit it.

ingredients.name: Fermented milk
ingredients.summary: Dairy ingredient that has been fermented by beneficial bacteria, similar to yogurt or kefir.
ingredients.details: Fermented milk can provide protein, calcium, and potentially beneficial probiotics that support gut health. It is generally safe but is an allergen for people with milk/dairy allergy or lactose intolerance, who may experience digestive or immune reactions.

ingredients.name: Citric acid
ingredients.summary: Common food acid and preservative used to adjust acidity and improve shelf life.
ingredients.details: Citric acid is widely used in foods and beverages and is considered safe for most people at typical intake levels. A small number of individuals may experience mouth irritation or report sensitivity, but it is not generally associated with serious health risks.

ingredients.name: Mono- and diglycerides
ingredients.summary: Emulsifiers derived from fats, used to blend water and oil and improve texture.
ingredients.details: Mono- and diglycerides are processed fat-based additives that can be sourced from vegetable oils or animal fats and may contain small amounts of trans fats depending on processing. Regulatory agencies consider them safe at typical levels, but because they can contribute to overall fat and possible trans fat intake, people aiming to minimize ultra‑processed additives or trans fats may wish to limit them.

ingredients.name: Alkali
ingredients.summary: Alkali refers to basic (high pH) substances used in food processing, often to adjust acidity or modify texture and color. Common food-grade alkalis include sodium carbonate or potassium carbonate.
ingredients.details: In foods, alkalis are typically used in small, regulated amounts to control acidity, improve texture, or enhance color (for example, in cocoa or noodles). For most people, intake from processed foods is considered safe, though it can contribute slightly to overall sodium or mineral load depending on the specific alkali used. People with kidney disease or those on strict mineral-restricted diets should be mindful of cumulative intake from many processed foods.

ingredients.name: Tomato extract
ingredients.summary: Tomato extract is a concentrated form of tomato, providing flavor, color, and beneficial compounds like lycopene. It is generally considered safe and can have some nutritional benefits.
ingredients.details: Tomato extract is often used to intensify tomato flavor and color in sauces, soups, and snacks. It can be a source of antioxidants such as lycopene, which has been studied for potential heart and cancer-protective effects. The main concern is for individuals with tomato allergy or reflux/heartburn, as acidic tomato products can aggravate symptoms.

ingredients.name: Soy protein
ingredients.summary: Soy protein is a concentrated protein derived from soybeans, used to boost protein content and improve texture. It is a common allergen and must be avoided by people with soy allergy.
ingredients.details: Soy protein can be nutritionally beneficial as a complete plant protein and may support heart health when used in place of some animal proteins. However, soy is one of the major food allergens and can cause reactions ranging from mild (hives, digestive upset) to severe (anaphylaxis) in sensitive individuals. People with thyroid issues taking medication or with hormone-sensitive conditions sometimes choose to moderate high intakes of processed soy, though typical amounts in foods are generally considered safe for most consumers.

ingredients.name: Hydrolysate
ingredients.summary: Hydrolysate usually refers to protein that has been broken down into smaller peptides or amino acids to improve digestibility and flavor. It is generally safe but can be a hidden source of free glutamates and allergens depending on the source protein.
ingredients.details: Protein hydrolysates are made by enzymatically or chemically breaking down proteins from sources such as milk, soy, or wheat. While they can improve digestibility and are common in flavorings and processed foods, they may contribute additional free glutamate, which can act similarly to MSG in sensitive individuals. People with allergies to the source protein (e.g., milk, soy, gluten-containing grains) should be cautious if the source is not clearly labeled.

ingredients.name: Apple puree
ingredients.summary: Apple puree is a processed form of apples, providing natural sugars, fiber, and phytonutrients. It is generally safe and considered a whole‑food ingredient.
ingredients.details: Apple puree is made by cooking and blending apples, often retaining much of the fruit’s natural vitamins, minerals, and polyphenols, though fiber can be partially reduced depending on processing. It contributes natural sugars, which can affect blood glucose if eaten in large amounts, but is typically less concerning than refined sugars. People with specific fruit allergies or fructose malabsorption may need to monitor intake.

ingredients.name: Dried (dehydrated ingredient descriptor)
ingredients.summary: “Dried” here appears to be a processing descriptor indicating that one or more ingredients are dehydrated, not a separate additive. Drying itself does not usually pose a health risk.
ingredients.details: The term “dried” is commonly used on labels to indicate that ingredients such as fruits, vegetables, or dairy have had water removed to improve shelf life and stability. Drying can slightly reduce some heat‑sensitive vitamins but generally preserves most nutrients and does not introduce chemical hazards by itself. Any health impact is more related to the specific dried ingredient (e.g., dried fruit sugar concentration) than to the drying process.

ingredients.name: Maltose
ingredients.summary: Maltose is a disaccharide sugar used as a sweetener and can contribute to excess sugar intake and blood sugar elevation.
ingredients.details: Maltose is composed of two glucose units and is broken down quickly in the body, leading to a glycemic effect similar to other refined sugars. While safe in small amounts, regular high intake of maltose and other added sugars can promote dental caries, weight gain, and increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases.

ingredients.name: Whey powder
ingredients.summary: Whey powder is a dairy-derived protein ingredient that is nutritious but a common allergen and unsuitable for people with milk allergy.
ingredients.details: Whey is one of the main proteins in milk and is often used to boost protein content and improve texture and flavor. It is generally safe for most people but can trigger allergic reactions in those with cow’s milk allergy and may cause digestive discomfort in some individuals with lactose intolerance, depending on residual lactose content.

ingredients.name: Garlic flake
ingredients.summary: Garlic flake is dried garlic used for flavoring and has a similar health profile to fresh garlic.
ingredients.details: Dried garlic retains many of the flavor compounds and some of the bioactive sulfur compounds found in fresh garlic. It is generally safe, with similar potential benefits and cautions as fresh garlic, including possible digestive irritation or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: Paprika color
ingredients.summary: Paprika color is a natural colorant derived from paprika peppers, used to give a red or orange hue to foods.
ingredients.details: It contains carotenoid pigments such as capsanthin and capsorubin and is considered a natural alternative to synthetic dyes. It is generally safe, though individuals with allergies to peppers or nightshade vegetables could theoretically react, which is uncommon.

ingredients.name: Disodium inosinate
ingredients.summary: Disodium inosinate is a flavor enhancer often used with monosodium glutamate (MSG) to intensify savory (umami) taste. It is generally recognized as safe but can be a concern for people sensitive to flavor enhancers or trying to avoid ultra-processed foods.
ingredients.details: Disodium inosinate (E631) is a nucleotide-based flavor enhancer commonly added to snacks, soups, and instant foods to boost umami flavor. While toxicological data suggest it is safe at typical intake levels, it is usually a marker of highly processed foods and is often combined with MSG or other enhancers, which some individuals report sensitivity to (e.g., headaches, flushing). People with gout or high uric acid may wish to limit intake because it is related to purine metabolism, although usual dietary amounts are small.
